text:
Connor Bedard is doing his part. He has 17 points in 14 games, 3.52 points per 60 minutes, and 13 points in his last ten, close to what we'd expect at 20:55 a night. His goals match his chances almost exactly (6 on 5.9 expected), so nothing here is a mirage.

The problem is around him. Chicago won two of those ten games, and with Bedard on the ice at five on five the Blackhawks get only 43.2% of the expected goals. Evolving-Hockey's read on last season explains part of it: his teammates ranked in the bottom 2% by impact while he drew the 92nd percentile of competition, and opponents generated a lot against him. The headlines have turned to the coach, with Bedard saying the team has "100 percent belief" in Jeff Blashill (NHL.com).

What to watch: the top line just got shuffled, with Greenway in for Bertuzzi beside Bedard and Kantserov (Scott Powers, The Athletic). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him among the best at getting to the slot. He'll keep getting there. Whether anyone joins him is Chicago's question.
headline: Bedard is producing on a team that keeps losing
